chunks.label: Zero to five
chunks.rationale: Lets you count and read out numbers up to five.
chunks.interference: Yon and shi both mean four; say yon.

chunks.label: Six to ten
chunks.rationale: Lets you count to ten and say times and ages.
chunks.interference: Nana and shichi both mean seven, kyuu and ku both nine; shichi sounds like ichi.

chunks.label: Building bigger numbers
chunks.rationale: Lets you say any number up to 9,999.
chunks.interference: Juuni (12) and nijuu (20) swap the same two parts.

chunks.label: Changed hundreds and thousands
chunks.rationale: Lets you say prices like 300 or 8,000 yen correctly.
chunks.interference: Saying the regular rokuhyaku or hachisen instead of the changed forms.

chunks.label: Big numbers in man
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about rent, salaries and big prices.
chunks.interference: English counts in thousands; 100,000 is juuman, not hyakusen.

chunks.label: Things one to five
chunks.rationale: Lets you count and order things without knowing a counter.
chunks.interference: Hitotsu and futatsu are things; hitori and futari are people.

chunks.label: Things six to ten
chunks.rationale: Lets you count things up to ten.
chunks.interference: Muttsu (6) sounds like mittsu (3), and yattsu (8) like yottsu (4).

chunks.label: Asking how many
chunks.rationale: Lets you ask how many, say 'a few' and go through things one by one.
chunks.interference: Ikutsu asks how many; ikutsuka means a few.

chunks.label: Counting people
chunks.rationale: Lets you say and ask how many people, as at a restaurant door.
chunks.interference: One and two people are hitori and futari, not ichinin and ninin; four is yonin.

chunks.label: Both, each, only one
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about both people, each person, a lone person and the headcount.
chunks.interference: Hitori hitori (each person) vs hitotsu hitotsu (each thing).
